title.zh: 卷七十四 四夷附錄第三: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城
title.en: Volume 74: Appendix on the Four Barbarians 3: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Tujie, Tubo, Huihu, Yutian, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Tungusic Tribes, Nanzhao Man, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa
title.raw: 卷七十四 四夷附錄第三: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城 Volume 74: Appendix on the Four Barbarians 3: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Tujie, Tubo, Huihu, Yutian, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Tungusic Tribes, Nanzhao Man, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa

sentences.zh: 奚 吐渾 達靼 党項 突厥 吐蕃 回鶻 于闐 高麗 渤海 新羅 黑水靺鞨 南詔蠻 牂牁 昆明 占城

translations.literal: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turk, Tibet, Uyghur, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Tuyuhun, Dada, Tangut, Turks, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Khotan, Goryeo, Bohai, Silla, Heishui Mohe, Nanzhao, Zhangke, Kunming, and Champa.

sentences.zh: 奚，本匈奴之別種。

translations.literal: The Xi were originally a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were originally a distinct offshoot of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 當唐之末，居陰涼川，在營府之西，幽州之西南，皆數百里。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang they dwelt on the Yinliang River, several hundred li west of Ying Prefecture and southwest of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Tang dynasty they lived along the Yinliang River, several hundred li west of Ying Prefecture and southwest of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 有人馬二萬騎。

translations.literal: They had twenty thousand men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They could field twenty thousand mounted warriors.

sentences.zh: 分爲五部：一曰阿薈部，二曰啜米部，三曰粵質部，四曰奴皆部，五曰黑訖支部。

translations.literal: They were divided into five sections: first the Ahui section, second the Chuomi section, third the Yuezhi section, fourth the Nujie section, and fifth the Heiqizhi section.
translations.idiomatic: They were organized in five divisions: the Ahui, Chuomi, Yuezhi, Nujie, and Heiqizhi tribes.

sentences.zh: 後徙居琵琶川，在幽州東北數百里。

translations.literal: Later they moved to the Pipa River, several hundred li northeast of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They later relocated to the Pipa River region, several hundred li northeast of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 地多黑羊，馬嵒前蹄堅善走，其登山逐獸，下上如飛。

translations.literal: The land had many black sheep; their horses had hard front hooves and ran well; climbing mountains to pursue game they went up and down like flying.
translations.idiomatic: Black sheep were plentiful there, and their horses had tough forehooves and great speed; in the mountains they chased game up and down slopes as if in flight.

sentences.zh: 契丹阿保機強盛，室韋、奚、霫皆服屬之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Abaoji grew powerful, the Shiwei, Xi, and Xi (Mohe) all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan leader Abaoji rose to power, the Shiwei, Xi, and Xi tribes all submitted to his rule.

sentences.zh: 奚人常爲契丹守界上，而苦其苛虐，奚王去諸怨叛，以別部西徙媯州，依北山射獵，常采北山麝香、仁參賂劉守光以自托。

translations.literal: The Xi often guarded the border for the Khitan and suffered their harsh cruelty; the Xi king Quzhu resented this and rebelled, leading a separate branch west to Gui Prefecture, relying on the northern mountains for hunting, and often gathering musk and ginseng from those mountains to bribe Liu Shouguang for protection.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were often made to guard the frontier for the Khitan and groaned under their harsh rule. King Quzhu of the Xi rebelled in anger, led a splinter group west to Gui Prefecture, and lived by hunting in the northern hills, regularly sending musk and ginseng from those hills to Liu Shouguang as gifts to win his protection.

sentences.zh: 其族至數千帳，始分爲東、西奚。

translations.literal: Their clans reached several thousand tents and first divided into Eastern and Western Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Their people grew to several thousand tents and first split into Eastern and Western Xi.

sentences.zh: 去諸之族，頗知耕種，歲借邊民荒地種穄，秋熟則來獲，窖之山下，人莫知其處。

translations.literal: Quzhu's people came to know farming; each year they borrowed wasteland from border Chinese to plant millet, and when it ripened in autumn they came to harvest and stored it in pits in the mountains—no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhu's followers learned something of agriculture: each year they borrowed fallow land from border settlers to sow millet, returned in autumn to reap it, and cached the grain in mountain pits whose locations outsiders could not find.

sentences.zh: 爨以平底瓦鼎，煮穄爲粥，以寒水解之而飲。

translations.literal: They cooked millet into porridge in flat-bottomed tile cauldrons and drank it thinned with cold water.
translations.idiomatic: They boiled millet into gruel in flat-bottomed earthen pots and drank it diluted with cold water.

sentences.zh: 去諸卒，子掃剌立。

translations.literal: When Quzhu died, his son Saoci succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Quzhu died, his son Saoci took his place.

sentences.zh: 莊宗破劉守光，賜掃剌姓李，更其名紹威。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong defeated Liu Shouguang, he bestowed the surname Li on Saoci and changed his name to Shaowei.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong crushed Liu Shouguang, he granted Saoci the surname Li and renamed him Shaowei.

sentences.zh: 紹威卒，子拽剌立。

translations.literal: When Shaowei died, his son Zhuaili succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaowei died, his son Zhuaili succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 同光以後，紹威父子數遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: After the Tongguang era, Shaowei and his son repeatedly sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tongguang reign onward, Shaowei and his son sent envoys to court again and again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，紹威娶契丹女舍利逐不魯之姊爲妻，後逐不魯叛亡入西奚，紹威納之。

translations.literal: At first Shaowei took as wife the sister of the Khitan woman Shelizhu Bulu; later when Bulu rebelled and fled into Western Xi, Shaowei took her in.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei had first married the sister of the Khitan woman Shelizhu Bulu; when Bulu later rebelled and fled to Western Xi, Shaowei took her as his wife as well.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入立，割幽州雁門以北入於契丹，是時紹威與逐不魯皆已死，耶律德光已立晉北歸，拽剌迎謁馬前，德光曰：「非爾罪也。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, the lands north of Youzhou and Yanmen were ceded to the Khitan; by then both Shaowei and Bulu were dead; Yelü Deguang had already established Jin and was returning north; Zhuaili met him before his horse; Deguang said: "It is not your fault.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Later Jin came to power, everything north of Youzhou and Yanmen was ceded to the Khitan. By then Shaowei and Bulu were both dead. Yelü Deguang, having set up Jin, was marching north again; Zhuaili met him at his horse. Deguang said, "This is not your fault.

sentences.zh: 負我者，掃剌與逐不魯爾。」

translations.literal: Those who wronged me are Saoci and Bulu.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wronged me are Saoci and Bulu.

sentences.zh: 乃發其墓，粉其骨而揚之。

translations.literal: He then disinterred their tombs, ground their bones to powder, and scattered them.
translations.idiomatic: He then had their graves opened, their bones ground to dust, and the dust cast to the winds.

sentences.zh: 後德光滅晉，拽剌常以兵從。

translations.literal: Later when Deguang destroyed Jin, Zhuaili often followed with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Deguang overthrew Jin, Zhuaili regularly marched with his forces in attendance.

sentences.zh: 其後不復見於中國。

translations.literal: After that they were no longer seen in China.
translations.idiomatic: After that they disappear from the Chinese record.

sentences.zh: 自去諸徙媯州，自別爲西奚，而東奚在琵琶川者，亦爲契丹所並，不復能自見云。

translations.literal: Since Quzhu moved to Gui Prefecture and separated as Western Xi, the Eastern Xi who remained on the Pipa River were also absorbed by the Khitan and could no longer maintain themselves, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Once Quzhu moved to Gui Prefecture and the Western Xi stood apart, the Eastern Xi on the Pipa River were likewise swallowed up by the Khitan and could no longer hold their own, or so it is said.

sentences.zh: 吐渾，本號吐谷渾，或曰乞伏乾歸之苗裔。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun were originally called Tuyühun; some say they were descendants of Qifu Gangui.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun were originally known as the Tuyühun; some hold that they were descendants of Qifu Gangui.

sentences.zh: 自後魏以來，名見中國，居於青海之上。

translations.literal: From the Northern Wei onward their name appears in China; they dwelt above Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: From the Northern Wei period onward they appear in Chinese sources, living around Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 當唐至德中，爲吐蕃所攻，部族分散，其內附者，唐處之河西。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era of Tang they were attacked by Tibet; their tribes scattered, and those who submitted inward were settled by Tang west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's Zhide reign they were attacked by Tibet, their tribes scattered, and those who submitted were resettled by the Tang west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 其大姓有慕容、拓拔、赫連等族。

translations.literal: Their great clans included the Murong, Tuoba, Helian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Among their leading clans were the Murong, Tuoba, Helian, and others.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，首領赫連鐸爲陰山府都督，與討龐勳，以功拜大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yizong's time the leader Helian Duo was military commissioner of Yinshan Prefecture; he joined in suppressing Pang Xun and for his merit was appointed military governor of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yizong the chieftain Helian Duo served as commissioner of Yinshan Prefecture, helped put down Pang Xun, and was rewarded with the Datong military governorship.

sentences.zh: 爲晉王所破，其部族益微，散處蔚州界中。

translations.literal: He was defeated by the Prince of Jin; their tribes grew ever weaker and scattered within the borders of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated by the Prince of Jin, their people grew weaker still and scattered through the Wei Prefecture frontier.

sentences.zh: 莊宗時，有首領白承福者，依中山北石門爲柵，莊宗爲置寧朔、奉化兩府，以承福爲都督，賜其姓名爲李紹魯。

translations.literal: In Zhuangzong's time there was a leader Bai Chengfu who relied on Shimen north of Zhongshan as a stockade; Zhuangzong established the Ningshuo and Fenghua prefectures, made Chengfu commissioner, and bestowed on him the surname and personal name Li Shaolu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong a chieftain named Bai Chengfu fortified himself at Shimen north of Zhongshan. Zhuangzong set up the Ningshuo and Fenghua prefectures, appointed Chengfu commissioner, and gave him the Chinese name Li Shaolu.

sentences.zh: 終唐時，常遣使朝貢中國。

translations.literal: Throughout Tang they often sent envoys to pay court tribute to China.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tang period they regularly sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖立，割雁門以北入於契丹，於是吐渾爲契丹役屬，而苦其苛暴。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, the lands north of Yanmen were ceded to the Khitan; the Tuyuhun then became subject to Khitan service and suffered their harsh cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Later Jin came to power and ceded everything north of Yanmen to the Khitan, the Tuyuhun fell under Khitan domination and chafed at their brutal rule.

sentences.zh: 是時，安重榮鎮成德，有異志，陰遣人招吐渾入塞，承福等乃自五台入處中國。

translations.literal: At that time An Chongrong held Chengde and harbored disloyal designs; he secretly sent men to summon the Tuyuhun into the passes, and Chengfu and others then entered China from Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong, then military governor of Chengde, nursed rebellious ambitions and secretly invited the Tuyuhun across the border; Chengfu and his people entered Chinese territory by way of Wutai.

sentences.zh: 契丹耶律德光大怒，遣使者責誚高祖，高祖恐懼，遣供奉官張澄率兵搜索並、鎮、忻、代等州山谷中吐渾驅出之。

translations.literal: The Khitan Yelü Deguang was greatly angered and sent envoys to rebuke Gaozu; Gaozu was afraid and sent the palace attendant Zhang Cheng with troops to search the valleys of Bing, Zhen, Xin, Dai, and other prefectures and drive the Tuyuhun out.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Deguang flew into a rage and sent envoys to reproach Gaozu, who in fear dispatched the palace attendant Zhang Cheng with troops to scour the valleys of Bing, Zhen, Xin, Dai, and neighboring prefectures and drive the Tuyuhun back out.

sentences.zh: 然晉亦苦契丹，思得吐渾爲緩急之用，陰遣劉知遠鎮太原慰撫之。

translations.literal: Yet Jin also suffered from the Khitan and wished to keep the Tuyuhun as a force for emergencies; they secretly sent Liu Zhiyuan to garrison Taiyuan and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, too, was weary of the Khitan and hoped to keep the Tuyuhun as a reserve in crisis, so they quietly posted Liu Zhiyuan at Taiyuan to win them over.

sentences.zh: 終高祖時，承福數遣使者朝貢。

translations.literal: Throughout Gaozu's reign Chengfu repeatedly sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Gaozu's reign Chengfu sent tribute missions again and again.

sentences.zh: 後出帝與契丹絕盟，召承福入朝，拜大同軍節度使，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Later when Emperor Chudi broke the alliance with the Khitan, he summoned Chengfu to court, appointed him military governor of Datong, and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Chudi renounced the Khitan alliance, he summoned Chengfu to court, made him military governor of Datong, and treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 契丹與晉相距於河，承福以其兵從出帝禦虜。

translations.literal: The Khitan and Jin faced each other across the river; Chengfu followed Chudi with his troops to resist the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan and Jin faced off along the Yellow River, Chengfu marched with his men to aid Chudi against the invaders.

sentences.zh: 是歲大熱，吐渾多疾死，乃遣承福歸太原，居之嵐、石之間。

translations.literal: That year was intensely hot and many Tuyuhun died of disease; Chudi then sent Chengfu back to Taiyuan to dwell between Lan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That summer was fiercely hot and disease killed many Tuyuhun, so Chudi sent Chengfu back to Taiyuan to settle his people between Lan and Shi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠稍侵辱之，承福謀復亡出塞，知遠以兵圍其族，殺承福及其大姓赫連海龍、白可久、白鐵匱等，其羊馬貲財巨萬計，皆籍沒之，其餘衆以其別部王義宗主之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan gradually insulted and humiliated them; Chengfu plotted to flee beyond the passes again; Zhiyuan surrounded their clans with troops and killed Chengfu and the great-clan leaders Helian Hailong, Bai Kejiu, Bai Tiegui, and others; their sheep, horses, and goods numbering in the tens of thousands were all confiscated; the remaining people were placed under Wang Yizong of another branch.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan gradually bullied them until Chengfu planned to flee beyond the frontier again. Zhiyuan surrounded the tribe with troops, killed Chengfu and leading clansmen including Helian Hailong, Bai Kejiu, and Bai Tiegui, confiscated tens of thousands of head of livestock and vast stores of goods, and left the survivors under Wang Yizong of a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 吐渾遂微，不復見。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun then dwindled and were no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun thereafter faded from view.

sentences.zh: 初，唐以承福之族爲熟吐渾。

translations.literal: At first Tang called Chengfu's people the "settled" Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had first classified Chengfu's people as the "settled" Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 長興中，又有生吐渾杜每兒來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era there was also a "wild" Tuyuhun, Du Mei'er, who came to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing a "wild" Tuyuhun named Du Mei'er also came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 每兒，不知其國地、部族。

translations.literal: As for Mei'er, their homeland and tribe are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is known of Mei'er's homeland or tribal affiliation.

sentences.zh: 至漢乾祐二年，又有吐渾何戛剌來朝貢，不知爲生、熟吐渾，蓋皆微，不足考錄。

translations.literal: By the second year of Qianyou of Han there was also a Tuyuhun He Gela who came to pay tribute; whether he was "wild" or "settled" Tuyuhun is unknown—they were all so weak as to be unworthy of full record.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyou of Later Han another Tuyuhun, He Gela, came with tribute; whether he represented the wild or settled branch is unclear. By then they were all too insignificant to warrant detailed notice.

sentences.zh: 達靼，靺鞨之遺種，本在奚、契丹之東北，後爲契丹所攻，而部族分散，或屬契丹，或屬渤海，別部散居陰山者，自號達靼。

translations.literal: The Dada were a remnant of the Mohe, originally northeast of the Xi and Khitan; later attacked by the Khitan, their tribes scattered—some submitted to the Khitan, some to Bohai; a separate branch scattered in the Yinshan region called themselves Dada.
translations.idiomatic: The Dada were descendants of the Mohe who originally lived northeast of the Xi and Khitan. After Khitan attacks scattered them, some bands submitted to the Khitan and others to Bohai, while a separate group in the Yinshan region took the name Dada.

sentences.zh: 當唐末，以名見中國。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang their name appears in China.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Tang their name appears in Chinese records.

sentences.zh: 有每相溫、于越相溫，咸通中，從硃邪赤心討龐勳。

translations.literal: There were Meixiangwen and Yuyuexiangwen; in the Xiantong era they followed Zhuye Chixin in suppressing Pang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Leaders named Meixiangwen and Yuyuexiangwen marched with Zhuye Chixin against Pang Xun in the Xiantong period.

sentences.zh: 其後李國昌、克用父子爲赫連鐸等所敗，嘗亡入達靼。

translations.literal: Later when Li Guochang and his son Keyong were defeated by Helian Duo and others, they once fled into the Dada.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Guochang and his son Li Keyong were beaten by Helian Duo and others, they took refuge among the Dada.

sentences.zh: 後從克用入關破黃巢，由是居雲、代之間。

translations.literal: Later they followed Keyong through the passes to defeat Huang Chao and thereafter dwelt between Yun and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: They later followed Keyong east through the passes to crush Huang Chao and thereafter settled between Yun and Dai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其俗善騎射，畜多駝、馬。

translations.literal: Their custom was skilled riding and archery; their livestock were mostly camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They excelled at mounted archery and kept chiefly camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 其君長、部族名字，不可究見，惟其嘗通於中國者可見云。

translations.literal: The names of their chiefs and tribes cannot be fully traced; only those who had dealings with China can be seen, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The names of their chiefs and tribal divisions cannot all be recovered; only those who had contact with China are recorded.

sentences.zh: 同光中，都督折文逋數自河西來貢駝、馬。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era the commissioner Zhe Wenpu repeatedly came from west of the River with tribute of camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongguang the commissioner Zhe Wenpu repeatedly arrived from the Hexi region with camels and horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 明宗討王都於定州，都誘契丹入寇，明宗詔達靼入契丹界，以張軍勢，遣宿州刺史薛敬忠以所獲契丹團牌二百五十及弓箭數百賜雲州生界達靼，蓋唐常役屬之。

translations.literal: Mingzong campaigned against Wang Du at Dingzhou; Du induced the Khitan to invade; Mingzong ordered the Dada to enter Khitan territory to display military strength, and sent Suzhou prefect Xue Jingzhong to bestow on the Dada of the Yunzhou border two hundred fifty Khitan round shields captured in battle and several hundred bows and arrows—for Tang often kept them in subject service.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong attacked Wang Du at Dingzhou, Du drew the Khitan into the war. Mingzong ordered the Dada to raid Khitan territory to magnify his army's presence and sent Suzhou prefect Xue Jingzhong to reward the frontier Dada of Yunzhou with 250 captured Khitan round shields and hundreds of bows and arrows—Tang had long used them as auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 長興三年，首領頡哥率其族四百餘人來附。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing the leader Xiege led more than four hundred of his clansmen to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing the chieftain Xiege brought more than four hundred of his people to submit.

sentences.zh: 訖于顯德，常來不絕。

translations.literal: Down to Xiande they came without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Xiande reign their visits never stopped.

sentences.zh: 党項，西羌之遺種。

translations.literal: The Tangut were a remnant of the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut were descendants of the Western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 其國在《禹貢》析支之地，東至松州，西接葉護，南界春桑，北鄰吐渾，有地三千餘里。

translations.literal: Their country was in the land of Zhizhi in the Yugong; east to Song Prefecture, west bordering on Yehu, south bounded by Chunsang, north neighboring Tuyuhun—more than three thousand li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Their homeland lay in the Zhizhi region described in the Yugong: east to Song Prefecture, west to Yehu, south to Chunsang, north to Tuyuhun—more than three thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 無城邑而有室屋，以毛罽覆之。

translations.literal: They had no walled cities but had dwellings covered with felt.
translations.idiomatic: They built no walled towns but lived in felt-covered dwellings.

sentences.zh: 其人喜盜竊而多壽，往往百五六十歲。

translations.literal: Their people delighted in theft and lived long, often to one hundred fifty or sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: They were prone to raiding yet remarkably long-lived, often reaching one hundred fifty or sixty years.

sentences.zh: 其大姓有細封氏、費聽氏、折氏、野利氏，拓拔氏爲最強。

translations.literal: Their great clans included the Xifeng, Feiting, Zhe, and Yeli; the Tuoba were strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Their leading clans were the Xifeng, Feiting, Zhe, and Yeli, with the Tuoba the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 唐德宗時，党項諸部相率內附，居慶州者號東山部落，居夏州者號平夏部落。

translations.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time the Tangut tribes submitted inward in succession; those dwelling in Qing Prefecture were called the Eastern Mountain tribes, those in Xia Prefecture the Pingxia tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Dezong the Tangut tribes submitted in succession: those in Qing Prefecture were called the Eastern Mountain tribes, those in Xia Prefecture the Pingxia tribes.

sentences.zh: 部有大姓而無君長，不相統一，散處邠寧、鄜延、靈武、河西，東至麟、府之間。

translations.literal: The tribes had great clans but no paramount chief and were not unified, scattered through Binning, Fuyan, Lingwu, and Hexi, east to between Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Each tribe had its great clans but no single ruler; they were not united, and ranged from Binning, Fuyan, Lingwu, and the Hexi corridor east to Lin and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 自同光以後，大姓之強者各自來朝貢。

translations.literal: From Tongguang onward the powerful great clans each came to pay court tribute on their own.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongguang the strongest clans each sent their own tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，詔沿邊置場市馬，諸夷皆入市中國，而回鶻、党項馬最多。

translations.literal: In Mingzong's time an edict established border markets for horses; all the barbarians entered the markets of China, and Uyghur and Tangut horses were most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong ordered horse markets set up along the frontier; tribesmen of every kind traded in China, but Uyghur and Tangut horses predominated.

sentences.zh: 明宗招懷遠人，馬來無駑壯皆售，而所售常過直，往來館給，道路倍費。

translations.literal: Mingzong sought to win over distant peoples; when horses came, whether weak or strong all were bought, and the price paid often exceeded fair value; lodging and provisions on the road doubled the expense.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong courted distant peoples generously: every horse offered was purchased, sound or sorry, usually above market price, with lodging and rations on the road doubling the cost.

sentences.zh: 其每至京師，明宗爲御殿見之，勞以酒食，既醉，連袂歌呼，道其土風以爲樂，去又厚以賜賚，歲耗百萬計。

translations.literal: Whenever they reached the capital Mingzong received them in the main hall, entertained them with wine and food; once drunk they linked arms singing and shouting, telling of their native customs for amusement; on leaving they were richly rewarded—annual expenditure ran to a million.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they reached the capital Mingzong received them in the main hall with wine and food. Once drunk they would link arms, sing, and boast of their homelands for his amusement, then depart laden with gifts—costing more than a million a year.

sentences.zh: 唐大臣皆患之，數以爲言。

translations.literal: Tang ministers all worried over this and repeatedly spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ministers protested again and again at the expense.

sentences.zh: 乃詔吏就邊場售馬給直，止其來朝，而党項利其所得，來不可止。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered officials to buy horses at the border markets and pay fair price, stopping their coming to court—but the Tangut profited from what they received and their coming could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials to buy horses only at the border markets at fair prices and to end court visits, but the Tangut found the trade too profitable and kept coming anyway.

sentences.zh: 其在靈、慶之間者，數犯邊爲盜。

translations.literal: Those between Ling and Qing often raided the border as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Those between Lingwu and Qingzhou raided the frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 自河西回鶻朝貢中國，道其部落，輒邀劫之，執其使者，賣之他族，以易牛馬。

translations.literal: When the Hexi Uyghur paid tribute to China, passing through their tribes they would always intercept and rob them, seize their envoys, sell them to other peoples, and exchange for cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hexi Uyghur tribute missions passed through their lands they ambushed them, seized the envoys, sold them to other tribes, and traded the proceeds for cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣靈武康福、邠州藥彥稠等出兵討之。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent Kang Fu of Lingwu, Yao Yanchou of Bin Prefecture, and others with troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong dispatched Kang Fu of Lingwu, Yao Yanchou of Bin Prefecture, and others to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 福等擊破阿埋韋悉褒勒強賴埋廝骨尾及其大首領連香李八薩王、都統悉那埋摩、侍御乞埋嵬悉逋等族，殺數千人，獲其牛羊巨萬計，及其所劫外國寶玉等，悉以賜軍士。

translations.literal: Fu and the others defeated the tribes of Amai, Weixi, Baole, Qianglaimai, Siguwei, and their great chiefs Lianxiang, Li Basawang, the commander-in-chief Xinamaimo, the attendant Qimai Weixibu, and others, killing several thousand; they seized tens of thousands of their sheep and cattle and the foreign jewels they had robbed, all given to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's forces crushed the tribes of Amai, Weixi, Baole, Qianglaimai, Siguwei, and chiefs including Lianxiang, Li Basawang, Commander Xinamaimo, and Attendant Qimai Weixibu, killing thousands. Tens of thousands of sheep and cattle were seized, along with foreign gems they had plundered, and all were distributed to the troops.

sentences.zh: 由是党項之患稍息。

translations.literal: From this the Tangut trouble gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Tangut raids eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 至周太祖時，府州党項尼也六泥香王子、拓拔山等皆來朝貢。

translations.literal: By the time of Zhou Taizu, the Fuzhou Tangut Niyeliuni Xiangwangzi, Tuobashan, and others all came to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Taizu the Fuzhou Tangut leaders Niyeliuni Xiangwangzi, Tuobashan, and others came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年，慶州刺史郭彥欽貪其羊馬，侵擾諸部，獨野雞族強不可近，乃誣其族犯邊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun the Qingzhou prefect Guo Yanqin coveted their sheep and horses and harassed the tribes; only the Yaji tribe was strong and could not be approached, so he falsely accused that tribe of border violations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun Qingzhou prefect Guo Yanqin, greedy for their livestock, bullied the tribes. Only the Yaji clan was too strong to intimidate, so he falsely accused them of raiding the border.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使招慰之。

translations.literal: Taizu sent envoys to summon and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent envoys to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 野雞族苦彥欽，不肯聽命，太祖遣邠州折從阮、甯州刺史張建武等討之。

translations.literal: The Yaji tribe suffered under Yanqin and refused to obey; Taizu sent Zhe Congruan of Bin Prefecture, Zhang Jianwu the Ningzhou prefect, and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yaji, harried by Yanqin, refused to comply, so Taizu sent Zhe Congruan of Bin Prefecture, Ningzhou prefect Zhang Jianwu, and others against them.

sentences.zh: 建武勇於立功，不能通夷情，馳軍擊野雞族，殺數百人。

translations.literal: Jianwu was eager for merit but did not understand barbarian affairs; he galloped his army to strike the Yaji tribe and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu was bold in pursuit of glory but knew nothing of tribal ways; he charged the Yaji and killed several hundred.

sentences.zh: 而喜玉、折思、殺牛三族聞建武擊破野雞族，各以牛酒犒軍，軍士利其物，反劫掠之。

translations.literal: The Xiyu, Zhesi, and Shaniu tribes, hearing that Jianwu had defeated the Yaji, each brought cattle and wine to reward the army; the soldiers coveted their goods and in turn plundered them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiyu, Zhesi, and Shaniu clans heard that Jianwu had beaten the Yaji, they brought cattle and wine to feast the troops—but the soldiers coveted their goods and looted them instead.

sentences.zh: 三族共誘建武軍至包山，度險，三族共擊之，軍投崖谷，死傷甚衆。

translations.literal: The three tribes together lured Jianwu's army to Baoshan; crossing the dangerous ground, all three tribes attacked together; the army fell into cliffs and ravines and casualties were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The three clans lured Jianwu's army to Baoshan and, once he was on treacherous ground, attacked together. Many soldiers were driven over cliffs and ravines, and casualties were severe.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，罪建武等，選良吏爲慶州刺史以招撫之。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry and punished Jianwu and the others, selecting good officials as Qingzhou prefect to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was furious, punished Jianwu and his officers, and appointed capable men as Qingzhou prefect to pacify the tribes by diplomacy.

sentences.zh: 其他諸族，散處尚邊界上者甚衆，然其無國地、君長，故莫得而紀次云。

translations.literal: Other tribes scattered along the border were very numerous, yet they had no fixed territory or paramount chief, and so cannot be fully recorded, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Countless other tribes still dotted the frontier, but without fixed homelands or paramount rulers they cannot be set down in order.

sentences.zh: 突厥，國地、君世、部族、名號、物俗，見於唐著矣。

translations.literal: As for the Turks, their territory, rulers, tribes, titles, and customs are fully set forth in Tang records.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks' lands, royal lines, tribes, titles, and customs are already fully described in Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 至唐之末。

translations.literal: By the end of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 爲諸夷所侵，部族微散。

translations.literal: They were invaded by the various barbarians and their tribes dwindled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Other peoples pressed in on them until their tribes dwindled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 五代之際，嘗來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period they sometimes came to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties they still sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，渾解樓來。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Hun Jielou came.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang Hun Jielou arrived.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，首領張慕晉來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng the leader Zhang Mujin came.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng the chieftain Zhang Mujin came.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，首領杜阿熟來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing the leader Du Ashu came.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing the chieftain Du Ashu came.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，遣使者薛同海等來。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu they sent envoys Xue Tonghai and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu they sent envoys led by Xue Tonghai.

sentences.zh: 凡四至，其後不復來。

translations.literal: In all they came four times; after that they came no more.
translations.idiomatic: They came four times in all and never returned.

sentences.zh: 然突厥于時最微，又來不數，故其君長史皆失不能紀。

translations.literal: Yet the Turks were then weakest of all and came but seldom, so the records of their chiefs are lost and cannot be set down.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Turks were at their weakest and visited only rarely, so the names of their rulers have been lost beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃，國地、君世、部族、名號、物俗，見於唐著矣。

translations.literal: As for Tibet, their territory, rulers, tribes, titles, and customs are fully set forth in Tang records.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet's lands, royal lines, tribes, titles, and customs are already fully described in Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 當唐之盛時，河西、隴右三十三州，涼州最大，土沃物繁而人富樂。

translations.literal: When Tang was at its height, the thirty-three prefectures of Hexi and Longyou—Liangzhou the greatest—had fertile soil, abundant goods, and a prosperous, contented people.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of Tang power the thirty-three prefectures of Hexi and Longyou flourished, Liangzhou foremost among them, with rich soil, abundant goods, and a prosperous people.

sentences.zh: 其地宜馬，唐置八監，牧馬三十萬匹。

translations.literal: The land was suited to horses; Tang established eight stud farms and pastured three hundred thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The region was ideal for horses; Tang maintained eight stud farms there with three hundred thousand head.

sentences.zh: 以安西都護府羈縻西域三十六國。

translations.literal: Through the Protectorate General of Anxi they kept the thirty-six states of the Western Regions in loose allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Protectorate General of Anxi the Tang held the thirty-six states of the Western Regions in loose allegiance.

sentences.zh: 唐之軍、鎮、監、務，三百餘城，常以中國兵更戍，而涼州置使節度之。

translations.literal: Tang's armies, garrisons, stud farms, and offices numbered more than three hundred cities; Chinese troops were regularly rotated to garrison them, and Liangzhou had a commissioner to command the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred Tang garrisons, posts, stud farms, and offices dotted the region, manned by rotating Chinese troops under a military commissioner based at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山之亂，肅宗起靈武，悉召河西兵赴難，而吐蕃乘虛攻陷河西、隴右，華人百萬皆陷於虜。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion Emperor Suzong rose at Lingwu and summoned all Hexi troops to the rescue; Tibet seized the opportunity and attacked, taking Hexi and Longyou—a million Chinese fell into barbarian hands.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion Emperor Suzong rallied at Lingwu and called every Hexi soldier to the cause. Tibet struck while the frontier was bare, overran Hexi and Longyou, and a million Chinese subjects fell under Tibetan rule.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，嘗遣使者至西域，見甘、涼、瓜、沙等州城邑如故，而陷虜之人見唐使者，夾道迎呼，涕泣曰：「皇帝猶念陷蕃人民否？」

translations.literal: In Emperor Wenzong's time envoys were once sent to the Western Regions; they saw the cities of Gan, Liang, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures standing as before, but the people who had fallen to the barbarians, seeing Tang envoys, lined the roads welcoming and crying: "Does the Emperor still remember the people lost to Tibet?
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenzong envoys reached the Western Regions and found the cities of Gan, Liang, Gua, Sha, and the rest still standing—but Chinese who had fallen under Tibetan rule lined the roads to greet them in tears, crying, "Does the Emperor still remember those of us lost to Tibet?

sentences.zh: 其人皆天寶時陷虜者子孫，其語言稍變，而衣服猶不改。

translations.literal: Those people were all descendants of those who fell to the barbarians in the Tianbao era; their language had changed somewhat, but their clothing had not altered.
translations.idiomatic: They were all descendants of people lost to the invaders in the Tianbao reign; their speech had shifted somewhat, but they still dressed as before.

sentences.zh: 至五代時，吐蕃已微弱，回鶻、党項諸羌夷分侵其地，而不有其人民。

translations.literal: By the Five Dynasties period Tibet had already weakened; Uyghurs, Tangut, and various Qiang tribes invaded their lands in turn but did not hold their people.
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Dynasties Tibet had grown feeble; Uyghurs, Tangut, and other Qiang peoples carved up its territory but did not rule its population.

sentences.zh: 值中國衰亂，不能撫有，惟甘、涼、瓜、沙四州常自通於中國。

translations.literal: China was in decline and turmoil and could not govern them; only the four prefectures of Gan, Liang, Gua, and Sha maintained their own contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: With China in turmoil and unable to govern the region, only Gan, Liang, Gua, and Sha prefectures kept up regular contact on their own.

sentences.zh: 甘州爲回鶻牙，而涼、瓜、沙三州將吏，猶稱唐官，數來請命。

translations.literal: Ganzhou was the Uyghur headquarters, while the officials of Liang, Gua, and Sha still called themselves Tang officers and repeatedly came to request commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou served as the Uyghur capital, but officials in Liang, Gua, and Sha still styled themselves Tang appointees and repeatedly sought imperial commissions.

sentences.zh: 自梁太祖時，嘗以靈武節度使兼領河西節度，而觀察甘、肅、威等州。

translations.literal: From the time of Liang Taizu, the Lingwu military governor was sometimes also made Hexi military governor, overseeing Gan, Su, Wei, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang Taizu onward the Lingwu military governor sometimes doubled as Hexi military governor, with oversight of Gan, Su, Wei, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 然雖有其名，而涼州自立守將。

translations.literal: Yet though the title existed, Liangzhou maintained its own defending commander.
translations.idiomatic: The title existed in name only; Liangzhou kept its own local commander.

sentences.zh: 唐長興四年，涼州留後孫超遣大將拓拔承謙及僧、道士、耆老楊通信等至京師求旌節，明宗問孫超等世家，承謙曰：「吐蕃陷涼州，張掖人張義朝募兵擊走吐蕃，唐因以義朝爲節度使，發鄆州兵二千五百人戍之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Tang, Liangzhou acting governor Sun Chao sent the great general Tuoba Chengqian and monks, Daoist priests, and elder Yang Tongxin and others to the capital to request a commission; Mingzong asked about Sun Chao's lineage; Chengqian said: "When Tibet took Liangzhou, Zhang Yichao of Zhangye raised troops and drove the Tibetans away; Tang therefore made Yichao military governor and sent twenty-five hundred Yanzhou troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's fourth year of Changxing, acting governor Sun Chao of Liangzhou sent General Tuoba Chengqian, monks, Daoists, and elder Yang Tongxin to the capital for an imperial commission. When Mingzong asked about their origins, Chengqian explained: "After Tibet seized Liangzhou, Zhang Yichao of Zhangye raised troops and drove them out. Tang appointed Yichao military governor and sent twenty-five hundred men from Yanzhou to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 唐亡，天下亂，涼州以東爲突厥、党項所隔，鄆兵遂留不得返。

translations.literal: When Tang fell and the realm was in chaos, the lands east of Liangzhou were cut off by Turks and Tangut; the Yanzhou garrison could not return.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang's collapse the realm fell into chaos; Turks and Tangut blocked the route east from Liangzhou, and the Yanzhou garrison was stranded.

sentences.zh: 今涼州漢人，皆其戍人子孫也。」

translations.literal: The Chinese of Liangzhou today are all descendants of those garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Han population in Liangzhou are all descendants of that garrison.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃拜孫超節度使。

translations.literal: Mingzong then appointed Sun Chao military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then appointed Sun Chao military governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，留後李文謙來請命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai the acting governor Li Wenqian came to request a commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai acting governor Li Wenqian came to court for a commission.

sentences.zh: 後數年，涼州人逐出文謙，靈武馮暉遣牙將吳繼勳代文謙爲留後，是時天福七年。

translations.literal: Several years later the people of Liangzhou expelled Wenqian; Feng Hui of Lingwu sent his officer Wu Jixun to replace Wenqian as acting governor—this was the seventh year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later the people of Liangzhou drove out Wenqian. Feng Hui of Lingwu sent officer Wu Jixun to replace him as acting governor, in the seventh year of Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 明年，晉高祖遣涇州押牙陳延暉齎詔書安撫涼州，涼州人共劫留延暉，立以爲刺史。

translations.literal: The next year Jin Gaozu sent Jingzhou officer Chen Yanhui with an edict to pacify Liangzhou; the people of Liangzhou together detained Yanhui by force and installed him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Gaozu of Later Jin sent Jingzhou officer Chen Yanhui with an edict to reassure Liangzhou, but the locals seized him and made him their prefect.

sentences.zh: 至漢隱帝時，涼州留後折逋嘉施來請命，漢即以爲節度使。

translations.literal: By the time of Han Emperor Yindi, Liangzhou acting governor Zhebo Jiashi came to request a commission and Han immediately made him military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han's Emperor Yin, acting governor Zhebo Jiashi of Liangzhou came to court for a commission and was promptly appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 嘉施，土豪也。

translations.literal: Jiashi was a local strongman.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashi was a local magnate.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，嘉施遣人市馬京師，因來請命帥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, Jiashi sent men to buy horses in the capital and thereby came to request appointment as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's second year of Guangshun, Jiashi sent men to trade horses in the capital and used the occasion to request appointment as military governor.

sentences.zh: 是時，樞密使王峻用事。

translations.literal: At that time the commissioner of military affairs Wang Jun held power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Jun, commissioner of military affairs, dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 峻故人申師厚者，少起盜賊，爲兗州牙將，與峻相友善，後峻貴，師厚敝衣蓬首，日候峻出，拜馬前，訴以饑寒，峻未有以發。

translations.literal: Jun's old acquaintance Shen Shihou had risen from banditry in youth and become a Yanzhou officer; he and Jun were on friendly terms. After Jun rose high, Shihou in ragged clothes and unkempt hair daily waited for Jun to emerge, bowed before his horse, and complained of hunger and cold, but Jun had no way to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's old friend Shen Shihou had begun as a bandit and become an officer in Yanzhou; the two were close. Once Jun grew powerful, Shihou in rags and with matted hair waited daily at his gate, bowed before his horse, and begged relief from hunger and cold, but Jun had nothing to give him.

sentences.zh: 而嘉施等來請帥，峻即建言：「涼州深入夷狄，中國未嘗命吏，請募率府率、供奉官能往者。」

translations.literal: When Jiashi and others came to request a commander, Jun immediately proposed: "Liangzhou lies deep among the barbarians and China has never appointed officials there; let us recruit a director of the directorate and palace attendants willing to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiashi and others petitioned for a governor, Jun proposed at once: "Liangzhou lies deep in barbarian country and China has never posted officials there. Let us recruit a director of the directorate or palace attendants willing to go.

sentences.zh: 月餘，無應募者，乃奏起師厚爲左衛將軍，已而拜河西節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a month with no volunteers, he memorialized to recall Shihou as Left Guard general, and shortly after appointed him Hexi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After a month without volunteers he had Shihou recalled as a Left Guard general and soon appointed him Hexi military governor.

sentences.zh: 師厚至涼州，奏薦押衙副使崔虎心、陽妃谷首領沈念般等及中國留人子孫王廷翰、溫崇樂、劉少英爲將吏。

translations.literal: When Shihou reached Liangzhou he memorialized recommending the deputy escort commander Cui Huxin, the Yangfeigu chieftain Shen Nianban, and others, and the descendants of Chinese who had remained—Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying—as officers.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangzhou Shihou recommended deputy escort commander Cui Huxin, Yangfeigu chieftain Shen Nianban, and descendants of Chinese settlers Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying for military posts.

sentences.zh: 又自安國鎮至涼州，立三州以控扼諸羌，用其酋豪爲刺史。

translations.literal: He also from Anguo town to Liangzhou established three prefectures to control the various Qiang, appointing their chieftains as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Between Anguo and Liangzhou he set up three prefectures to control the Qiang tribes, naming tribal chiefs as prefects.

sentences.zh: 然涼州夷夏雜處，師厚小人，不能撫有。

translations.literal: Yet Liangzhou was a mixed barbarian and Chinese region, and Shihou was a petty man who could not govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou was a mixed frontier of barbarians and Chinese, and the petty Shihou could not govern it.

sentences.zh: 至世宗時，師厚留其子而逃歸，涼州遂絕於中國。

translations.literal: By Shizong's time Shihou left his son behind and fled back; Liangzhou was then cut off from China.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, Shihou abandoned his son and fled home, and Liangzhou was lost to China.

sentences.zh: 獨瓜、沙二州，終五代常來。

translations.literal: Only Gua and Sha prefectures came regularly throughout the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gua and Sha prefectures maintained contact throughout the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 沙州，梁開平中有節度使張奉，自號「金山白衣天子」。

translations.literal: At Sha Prefecture, in Liang's Kaiping era there was military governor Zhang Feng, who styled himself "White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: At Sha Prefecture, during Liang's Kaiping reign, military governor Zhang Feng styled himself the White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至唐莊宗時，回鶻來朝，沙州留後曹義金亦遣使附回鶻以來，莊宗拜義金爲歸義軍節度使、瓜沙等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: By Zhuangzong's time the Uyghur came to court; Sha Prefecture acting governor Cao Yijin also sent envoys attached to the Uyghur mission; Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military governor of the Guiyi Army and commissioner for Gua, Sha, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong the Uyghur came to court, and Sha's acting governor Cao Yijin sent envoys with their mission. Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military governor of the Guiyi Army and commissioner over Gua, Sha, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年，義金卒，子元德立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's fifth year of Tianfu, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 至七年，沙州曹元忠、瓜州曹元深皆遣使來。

translations.literal: By the seventh year, Cao Yuanzhong of Sha and Cao Yuanshen of Gua both sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh year Cao Yuanzhong of Sha and Cao Yuanshen of Gua both sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 周世宗時，又以元忠爲歸義軍節度使，元恭爲瓜州團練使。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time Yuanzhong was again made military governor of the Guiyi Army and Yuangong regimental commissioner of Gua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Shizong, Yuanzhong was again appointed military governor of the Guiyi Army and Yuangong regimental commissioner of Gua.

sentences.zh: 其所貢：硇砂、羚羊角、波斯錦、安西白灊、金星礬、胡桐律、大鵬砂、毦褐、玉團。

translations.literal: Their tribute items included sal ammoniac, antelope horns, Persian brocade, Anxi white felt, golden-star alum, diversifolious poplar, great-peng sand, felt rugs, and jade balls.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute included sal ammoniac, antelope horn, Persian brocade, Anxi white felt, golden-star alum, poplar products, mineral pigments, felt rugs, and jade ornaments.

sentences.zh: 皆因其來者以名見，而其卒立、世次，史皆失其紀。

translations.literal: All are known only by the names of those who came; their deaths, successions, and generations are lost from the records.
translations.idiomatic: We know them only through the names of visiting envoys; their successions and genealogies have been lost.

sentences.zh: 而吐蕃不見於梁世。

translations.literal: Tibet does not appear in the Liang period.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet does not appear in the records of the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 唐天成三年，回鶻王仁喻來朝，吐蕃亦遣使附以來，自此數至中國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Tang the Uyghur king Renyu came to court; Tibet also sent envoys attached to the mission, and from then on they came repeatedly to China.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's third year of Tiancheng the Uyghur king Renyu came to court, and Tibet sent envoys with his mission. After that they visited China repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘗禦端明殿見其使者，問其牙帳所居，曰：「西去涇州二千里。」

translations.literal: Mingzong once received their envoys in the Duanming Hall and asked where their headquarters lay; they said: "Two thousand li west of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong once received their envoys in the Duanming Hall and asked where their capital stood. They replied, "Two thousand li west of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明宗賜以虎皮，人一張，皆披以拜，委身宛轉，落其氈帽，亂髮如蓬，明宗及左右皆大笑。

translations.literal: Mingzong bestowed tiger skins, one per man; all draped them to bow, throwing themselves down and writhing; their felt hats fell off and their hair was tangled like rushes; Mingzong and those around him all laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong gave each man a tiger skin. They draped the skins to bow, prostrating and writhing until their felt hats fell off and their hair spilled out like tangled rushes. Mingzong and his attendants roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 至漢隱帝時猶來朝，後遂不復至，史亦失其君世云。

translations.literal: They still came to court in Yindi's time of Han; afterward they came no more, and the records of their rulers are lost, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: They still came under Later Han's Emperor Yin, but never returned afterward, and the succession of their rulers has been lost.

sentences.zh: 回鶻，爲唐患尤甚。

translations.literal: The Uyghur were an especially grave trouble to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Tang's frontier troubles, the Uyghur were among the gravest.

sentences.zh: 其國地、君世、物俗，見於唐著矣。

translations.literal: Their territory, rulers, and customs are fully set forth in Tang records.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands, rulers, and customs are already fully described in Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 唐嘗以女妻之，故其世以中國爲舅。

translations.literal: Tang once gave them princesses in marriage, so their generations called China "uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Tang had married princesses to their khans, so for generations they called China their uncle-by-marriage.

sentences.zh: 其國本在娑陵水上、後爲黠戛斯所侵，徙天德、振武之間，又爲石雄、張仲武所破，其餘衆西徙，役屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: Their state was originally on the Solon River; later attacked by the Kirghiz they moved between Tiande and Zhenwu; then defeated by Shi Xiong and Zhang Zhongwu, the remainder migrated west and became subject to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They had originally lived on the Solon River, but Kirghiz attacks drove them between Tiande and Zhenwu. Defeated by Shi Xiong and Zhang Zhongwu, the survivors moved west and fell under Tibetan domination.

sentences.zh: 是時吐蕃已陷河西、隴右，乃以回鶻散處之。

translations.literal: By then Tibet had already taken Hexi and Longyou and settled the scattered Uyghur there.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had already seized Hexi and Longyou and dispersed the Uyghur among those lands.

sentences.zh: 當五代之際，有居甘州、西州者嘗見中國，而甘州回鶻數至，猶呼中國爲舅，中國答以詔書亦呼爲甥。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period those dwelling in Ganzhou and Xizhou sometimes appeared in China; the Ganzhou Uyghur came repeatedly and still called China "uncle," and China in edicts replied calling them "nephew."
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties Uyghur in Ganzhou and Xizhou still had contact with China. The Ganzhou Uyghur visited often, still calling China uncle, and Chinese edicts addressed them as nephew in return.

sentences.zh: 梁乾化元年，遣都督周易言等來，而史不見其君長名號，梁拜易言等官爵，遣左監門衛上將軍楊沼押領還蕃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Liang they sent the commissioner Zhou Yiyan and others; the histories do not record their ruler's name and title; Liang bestowed offices on Yiyan and others and sent Left Gate Guard senior general Yang Zhao to escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's first year of Qianhua they sent Commissioner Zhou Yiyan and others, though the histories do not record their khan's name. Liang granted them titles and sent Senior General Yang Zhao of the Left Gate Guard to escort them home.

sentences.zh: 至唐莊宗時，王仁美遣使者來，貢玉、馬，自稱「權知可汗」，莊宗遣司農卿鄭續持節冊仁美爲英義可汗。

translations.literal: By Zhuangzong's time Wang Renmei sent envoys with tribute of jade and horses, styling himself "acting khan"; Zhuangzong sent Minister of Agriculture Zheng Xu with credentials to invest Renmei as Yingyi Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong, Wang Renmei sent envoys with jade and horses, styling himself acting khan. Zhuangzong dispatched Minister of Agriculture Zheng Xu to invest him as Yingyi Khan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，仁美卒，其弟狄銀立，遣都督安千想等來。

translations.literal: That year Renmei died; his brother Diyin succeeded and sent the commissioner An Qianxiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: That year Renmei died and his brother Diyin succeeded, sending Commissioner An Qianxiang and others to court.

sentences.zh: 同光四年，狄銀卒，阿咄欲立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang Diyin died and Adouyu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongguang Diyin died and Adouyu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，權知國事王仁裕遣李阿山等來朝，明宗遣使者冊仁裕爲順化可汗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng Wang Renyu, acting head of state affairs, sent Li Ashan and others to court; Mingzong sent envoys to invest Renyu as Shunhua Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng acting ruler Wang Renyu sent Li Ashan and others to court, and Mingzong invested him as Shunhua Khan.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時又冊爲奉化可汗。

translations.literal: In Jin Gaozu's time he was again invested as Fenghua Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu of Later Jin he was invested again as Fenghua Khan.

sentences.zh: 阿咄欲，不知其爲狄銀親疏，亦不知其立卒；

translations.literal: As for Adouyu, whether he was close or distant kin to Diyin is unknown, as are his accession and death;
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is known of Adouyu's relation to Diyin, or of his rise and fall;

sentences.zh: 而仁裕訖五代常來朝貢，史亦失其紀。

translations.literal: but Renyu came to pay tribute throughout the Five Dynasties, and the records of his line are also lost.
translations.idiomatic: but Renyu sent tribute throughout the Five Dynasties, and his genealogy, too, has been lost.

sentences.zh: 其地出玉、犛、綠野馬、獨峰駝、白貂鼠、羚羊角、硇砂、膃肭臍、金剛鑽、紅鹽、罽氎、騊駼之革。

translations.literal: Their land produced jade, yak, green wild horses, Bactrian camels, white sable, antelope horn, sal ammoniac, musk, diamond drills, red salt, felt rugs, and taotu leather.
translations.idiomatic: Their country yielded jade, yaks, green wild horses, Bactrian camels, white sable, antelope horn, sal ammoniac, musk, diamonds, red salt, felt rugs, and taotu leather.

sentences.zh: 其地宜白麥、青騑麥、黃麻、蔥韭、胡荽，以橐駝耕而種。

translations.literal: The land suited white wheat, blue wheat, yellow hemp, scallions, leeks, and coriander; they plowed and sowed with camels.
translations.idiomatic: The soil suited white and blue wheat, yellow hemp, scallions, leeks, and coriander, which they planted using camels to plow.

sentences.zh: 其可汗常樓居，妻號天公主，其國相號媚祿都督。

translations.literal: Their khan usually lived in a tower dwelling; his wife was styled Heavenly Princess; their chief minister was called Meilu Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Their khan usually lived in a tower house; his wife was called Heavenly Princess, and his chief minister Meilu Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 見可汗，則去帽被髮而入以爲禮。

translations.literal: When meeting the khan one removed one's hat, let down one's hair, and entered—that was the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To approach the khan one removed one's hat, unbound one's hair, and entered bareheaded—that was the custom.

sentences.zh: 婦人總發爲髻，高五六寸，以紅絹囊之；

translations.literal: Women bound their hair in a topknot five or six inches high and wrapped it in red silk;
translations.idiomatic: Women bound their hair in a topknot five or six inches high and wrapped it in red silk;

sentences.zh: 既嫁，則加氈帽。

translations.literal: once married they added a felt hat.
translations.idiomatic: after marriage they added a felt hat.

sentences.zh: 又有別族號龍家，其俗與回紇小異。

translations.literal: There was also a separate people called the Long family, whose customs differed slightly from the Uyghur.
translations.idiomatic: A separate people called the Long clan lived among them, with customs slightly different from the Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，回鶻來獻白鶻一聯，明宗命解緤放之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing the Uyghur presented a pair of white swans; Mingzong ordered the bindings removed and them released.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing the Uyghur presented a pair of white swans, and Mingzong ordered them unbound and set free.

sentences.zh: 自明宗時，常以馬市中國，其所齎寶玉皆屬縣官，而民犯禁爲市者輒罪之。

translations.literal: From Mingzong's time they often traded horses in China; the jade and gems they brought all belonged to the government, and commoners who violated the ban to trade were punished.
translations.idiomatic: From Mingzong's reign they traded horses regularly in China; jade and gems they brought were reserved for the state, and private trading was punished.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時除其禁，民得與回鶻私市，玉價由此倍賤。

translations.literal: In Zhou Taizu's time the ban was lifted; commoners could trade privately with the Uyghur, and jade prices thereby fell by half.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu lifted the ban, allowing private trade with the Uyghur, and jade prices fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，來獻玉，世宗曰：「玉雖寶而無益。」

translations.literal: In Xiande they came presenting jade; Shizong said: "Though jade is precious it is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande they brought jade as tribute. Shizong said, "Jade may be precious, but it is of no practical use.

sentences.zh: 卻之。

translations.literal: He declined it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 于闐，國地、君世、物俗見於唐。

translations.literal: As for Khotan, its territory, rulers, and customs appear in Tang records.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan's lands, rulers, and customs are described in Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 五代亂世，中國多故，不能撫來四夷。

translations.literal: In the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties China had many troubles and could not win over the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of the Five Dynasties China was preoccupied with internal crises and could not court the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 其嘗自通於中國者僅以名見，其君世、終始，皆不可知。

translations.literal: Those who had contact with China are known only by name; their rulers' generations and beginnings and ends are all unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Those who reached China are known only by name; their rulers' lines and histories are beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 而于闐尤遠，去京師萬里外。

translations.literal: Khotan was especially remote, more than ten thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan was the most distant of all, more than ten thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其國西南近蔥嶺，與婆羅門爲鄰國，而相去猶三千餘里，南接吐蕃，西北至疏勒二千餘里。

translations.literal: Their state in the southwest neared the Onion Mountains and bordered Brahman country, yet was still more than three thousand li apart; south it adjoined Tibet; northwest to Shule was more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest it lay near the Onion Mountains and bordered India, though still three thousand li away; south it met Tibet, and northwest Shule lay more than two thousand li distant.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，于闐國王李聖天遣使者馬繼榮來貢紅鹽、郁金、氂牛尾、玉灊等，晉遣供奉官張匡鄴假鴻臚卿，彰武軍節度判官高居誨爲判官，冊聖天爲大寶于闐國王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu of Jin, Khotan king Li Shengtian sent envoy Ma Jirong with tribute of red salt, turmeric, yak tails, jade felt, and the like; Jin sent palace attendant Zhang Kuangye acting as Director of Ceremonial, and Zhangwu circuit military governor's aide Gao Juhui as vice commissioner, to invest Shengtian as king of Great Treasure Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's third year of Tianfu, King Li Shengtian of Khotan sent Ma Jirong with red salt, turmeric, yak tails, jade felt, and other goods. Jin dispatched palace attendant Zhang Kuangye as acting Director of Ceremonial and Zhangwu circuit aide Gao Juhui as vice commissioner to invest Shengtian as King of Great Treasure Khotan.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬十二月，匡鄴等自靈州行二歲至于闐，至七年冬乃還。

translations.literal: That winter in the twelfth month Kuangye and the others set out from Ling Prefecture; after two years they reached Khotan, and returned only in the winter of the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the twelfth month, Kuangye's party left Ling Prefecture. Two years later they reached Khotan and did not return until the winter of the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 而居誨頗記其往復所見山川諸國，而不能道聖天世次也。

translations.literal: Gao Juhui recorded rather fully the mountains, rivers, and states seen on the journey there and back, but could not set forth Shengtian's genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Juhui left a detailed account of the lands and peoples he saw on the journey, but could not trace Shengtian's royal line.

sentences.zh: 居誨記曰：「自靈州過黃河，行三十里，始涉沙入党項界，曰細腰沙、神點沙。

translations.literal: Juhui's account says: "From Ling Prefecture crossing the Yellow River, after thirty li one first entered the sands into Tangut territory, called Narrow-Waist Sand and Spirit-Point Sand.
translations.idiomatic: Juhui wrote: "From Ling Prefecture we crossed the Yellow River; after thirty li we entered the sands and Tangut territory—Narrow-Waist Sand and Spirit-Point Sand.

sentences.zh: 至三公沙，宿月支都督帳。

translations.literal: Reaching Three-Lord Sand, they lodged at the Yuezhi commissioner's camp.
translations.idiomatic: At Three-Lord Sand we lodged in the Yuezhi commissioner's camp.

sentences.zh: 自此沙行四百餘里，至黑堡沙，沙尤廣，遂登沙嶺。

translations.literal: From there traveling the sands more than four hundred li they reached Black Fort Sand; the sands were especially vast, and they then ascended Sand Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: From there we crossed more than four hundred li of sand to Black Fort Sand, where the desert widened still further, and climbed Sand Ridge.

sentences.zh: 沙嶺，党項牙也，其酋曰撚崖天子。

translations.literal: Sand Ridge was a Tangut headquarters; their chieftain was called Nianya Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Sand Ridge was a Tangut headquarters, ruled by a chieftain called Nianya Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 渡白亭河至涼州，自涼州西行五百里至甘州。

translations.literal: Crossing the Baiting River they reached Liangzhou; from Liangzhou west five hundred li to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: We crossed the Baiting River to Liangzhou, then traveled five hundred li west to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 甘州，回鶻牙也。

translations.literal: Ganzhou was the Uyghur headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou was the Uyghur capital.

sentences.zh: 其南，山百餘里，漢小月支之故地也，有別族號鹿角山沙陀，雲硃耶氏之遺族也。

translations.literal: South of it, a hundred-odd li of mountains, was the old land of the Lesser Yuezhi of Han; there was a separate people called the Antler Mountain Shatuo, said to be remnants of the Zhuye clan.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li south lay the old homeland of the Lesser Yuezhi; there lived a people called the Antler Mountain Shatuo, said to be descendants of the Zhuye clan.

sentences.zh: 自甘州西，始涉磧。

translations.literal: West from Ganzhou they first entered the desert.
translations.idiomatic: West of Ganzhou we entered the desert proper.

sentences.zh: 磧無水，載水以行。

translations.literal: The desert had no water; they carried water to travel.
translations.idiomatic: The desert had no water; we had to carry supplies to survive.

sentences.zh: 甘州人教晉使者作馬蹄木澀，木澀四竅，馬蹄亦鑿四竅而綴之，駝蹄則包以氂皮乃可行。

translations.literal: The people of Ganzhou taught the Jin envoys to make wooden hoof-grips; the grips had four holes, and horse hooves were also bored with four holes and fitted to them; camel hooves were wrapped in felt before they could travel.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou locals taught the Jin envoys to make wooden hoof grips with four holes, fitted to horses whose hooves were bored to match; camels' hooves had to be wrapped in felt before they could cross the sands.

sentences.zh: 西北五百里至肅州，渡金河，西百里出天門關，又西百里出玉門關，經吐蕃界。

translations.literal: Five hundred li northwest to Suzhou; crossing the Golden River, a hundred li west out through Heavenly Gate Pass, another hundred li west out through Jade Gate Pass, passing through Tibetan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li northwest brought us to Suzhou. We crossed the Golden River, passed Heavenly Gate Pass a hundred li west, then Jade Gate Pass another hundred li west, crossing Tibetan territory.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃男子冠中國帽，婦人辮髪，戴瑟瑟珠，雲珠之好者，一珠易一良馬。

translations.literal: Tibetan men wore Chinese-style caps; women braided their hair and wore sese beads—it is said a fine bead could be exchanged for a good horse.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan men wore Chinese-style caps; women braided their hair and wore sese beads, said to be so fine that one bead could trade for a good horse.

sentences.zh: 西至瓜州、沙州，二州多中國人，聞晉使者來，其刺史曹元深等郊迎，問使者天子起居。

translations.literal: West to Gua and Sha prefectures; both had many Chinese; hearing Jin envoys were coming, their prefects Cao Yuanshen and others met them in the suburbs and asked after the Son of Heaven's health.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west lay Gua and Sha, where many Chinese still lived. Hearing of the Jin mission, prefects including Cao Yuanshen met them outside the walls and inquired after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 瓜州南十里鳴沙山，雲冬夏殷殷有聲如雷，雲《禹貢》流沙也。

translations.literal: Ten li south of Gua Prefecture was Singing Sand Mountain; it is said that winter and summer it rumbled like thunder—it is said to be the flowing sands of the Yugong.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li south of Gua stood Singing Sand Mountain, which rumbled winter and summer like thunder—identified with the flowing sands of the Yugong.

sentences.zh: 又東南十里三危山，雲三苗之所竄也。

translations.literal: Ten li southeast was Sanwei Mountain; it is said to be where the Three Miao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li southeast stood Sanwei Mountain, said to be where the Three Miao took refuge.

sentences.zh: 其西，渡都鄉河曰陽關。

translations.literal: West of it, crossing the Duxiang River was Yang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Westward, crossing the Duxiang River, lay Yang Pass.

sentences.zh: 沙州西曰仲雲，其牙帳居胡盧磧。

translations.literal: West of Sha Prefecture was called Zhongyun; their headquarters lay in Hulü Desert.
translations.idiomatic: West of Sha lay the land of Zhongyun, whose headquarters stood in Hulü Desert.

sentences.zh: 雲仲雲者，小月支之遺種也，其人勇而好戰，瓜、沙之人皆憚之。

translations.literal: It is said the Zhongyun were remnants of the Lesser Yuezhi; their people were brave and warlike, and the people of Gua and Sha all feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongyun were said to be descendants of the Lesser Yuezhi—fierce warriors whom the people of Gua and Sha all feared.

sentences.zh: 胡盧磧，漢明帝時征匈奴，屯田于吾盧，蓋其地也。

translations.literal: Hulü Desert—in Emperor Ming of Han's campaign against the Xiongnu, garrison farming was done at Wulu; this is probably that place.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Desert was probably the site where Emperor Ming of Han garrisoned troops at Wulu during his campaign against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 地無水而嘗寒多雪，每天暖雪銷，乃得水。

translations.literal: The land had no water and was always cold with much snow; only when the weather warmed and snow melted was there water.
translations.idiomatic: The land had no standing water and was bitterly cold with heavy snow; water came only when warm weather melted the snow.

sentences.zh: 匡鄴等西行入仲雲界，至大屯城，仲雲遣宰相四人、都督三十七人候晉使者，匡鄴等以詔書慰諭之，皆東向拜。

translations.literal: Kuangye and the others traveled west into Zhongyun territory to Datun city; Zhongyun sent four chancellors and thirty-seven commissioners to await the Jin envoys; Kuangye and the others comforted them with the edict, and all bowed facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangye's party traveled west into Zhongyun territory to Datun, where four chancellors and thirty-seven commissioners awaited them. Kuangye read the imperial edict of reassurance, and all bowed toward the east.

sentences.zh: 自仲雲界西，始涉𨢑磧，無水，掘地得濕沙，人置之胸以止渴。

translations.literal: West from Zhongyun territory they first entered salt desert; there was no water; digging the ground they got damp sand, which men placed on their chests to quench thirst.
translations.idiomatic: West of Zhongyun they entered the salt desert, where there was no water. Travelers dug up damp sand and pressed it to their chests to slake their thirst.

sentences.zh: 又西，渡陷河，伐檉置水中乃渡，不然則陷。

translations.literal: Farther west they crossed the Sinking River; they cut tamarisk and placed it in the water before crossing—otherwise they would sink.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west they crossed the Sinking River, laying cut tamarisk in the water to bear their weight—without it they would sink through.

sentences.zh: 又西，至紺州。

translations.literal: Farther west they reached Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Still farther west they came to Gan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紺州，于闐所置也，在沙州西南，雲去京師九千五百里矣。

translations.literal: Gan Prefecture was established by Khotan, southwest of Sha Prefecture; it is said to be nine thousand five hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Prefecture, established by Khotan southwest of Sha, was said to lie nine thousand five hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 又行二日至安軍州，遂至于闐。

translations.literal: After two more days' travel they reached Anjun Prefecture, and then arrived at Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they reached Anjun Prefecture and at last arrived in Khotan.

sentences.zh: 聖天衣冠如中國，其殿皆東向，曰金冊殿，有樓曰七鳳樓。

translations.literal: Shengtian's dress was like China's; his halls all faced east, called the Golden Book Hall, with a tower called the Seven Phoenix Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Shengtian dressed in Chinese style. His halls faced east—the Golden Book Hall—and he had a tower called the Seven Phoenix Tower.

sentences.zh: 以蒲桃爲酒，又有紫酒、青酒，不知其所釀，而味尤美。

translations.literal: They made wine from grapes; there were also purple wine and green wine—what they were brewed from is unknown, but the taste was especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: They made wine from grapes, and also purple and green wines of unknown ingredients, all exceptionally fine in flavor.

sentences.zh: 其食，粳沃以蜜，粟沃以酪。

translations.literal: Their food: polished rice moistened with honey, millet moistened with curds.
translations.idiomatic: They ate polished rice sweetened with honey and millet mixed with curds.

sentences.zh: 其衣布帛。

translations.literal: They wore cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: They dressed in cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 有園圃花木。

translations.literal: They had gardens and flowering trees.
translations.idiomatic: They kept gardens and flowering plants.

sentences.zh: 俗喜鬼神而好佛。

translations.literal: Their custom favored spirits and ghosts and they loved Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: They venerated spirits and were devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 聖天居處，嘗以紫衣僧五十人列侍，其年號同慶二十九年。

translations.literal: At Shengtian's residence fifty purple-robed monks once stood in attendance in ranks; his reign era was Tongqing, year twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At his court Shengtian kept fifty purple-robed monks in attendance. His reign title was Tongqing, in its twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 其國東南曰銀州、盧州、湄州，其南千三百里曰玉州，雲漢張騫所窮河源出于闐，而山多玉者此山也。」

translations.literal: Southeast of their state were Yin, Lu, and Mei prefectures; thirteen hundred li south was Yu Prefecture—it is said that the source of the river Zhang Qian of Han traced to its end was in Khotan, and this is the mountain rich in jade.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast lay Yin, Lu, and Mei prefectures; thirteen hundred li south stood Yu Prefecture, said to be the jade-rich mountain where Zhang Qian of Han found the river's source in Khotan.

sentences.zh: 其河源所出，至于闐分爲三：東曰白玉河，西曰綠玉河，又西曰烏玉河。

translations.literal: Where the river source emerges, reaching Khotan it divides into three: east called White Jade River, west called Green Jade River, and farther west Black Jade River.
translations.idiomatic: At its source the river splits into three branches in Khotan: the White Jade River to the east, the Green Jade River to the west, and the Black Jade River farther west.

sentences.zh: 三河皆有玉而色異，每歲秋水涸，國王撈玉于河，然後國人得撈玉。

translations.literal: All three rivers had jade but of different colors; each year when autumn waters receded the king gathered jade from the rivers, and only then could the people gather jade.
translations.idiomatic: All three rivers yielded jade of different colors. Each autumn, when the waters fell, the king gathered jade first; only afterward could the people do so.

sentences.zh: 自靈州渡黃河至于闐，往往見吐蕃族帳，而于闐常與吐蕃相攻劫。

translations.literal: From Ling Prefecture crossing the Yellow River to Khotan one often saw Tibetan encampments, and Khotan frequently raided and fought with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: From Ling Prefecture to Khotan one passed many Tibetan camps, and Khotan was often at war with Tibet, raiding back and forth.

sentences.zh: 匡鄴等至于闐，聖天頗責誚之，以邀誓約。

translations.literal: When Kuangye and the others reached Khotan, Shengtian rebuked them rather sharply to extract a sworn pact.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuangye's party arrived, Shengtian rebuked them harshly to extract a sworn agreement.

sentences.zh: 匡鄴等還，聖天又遣都督劉再升獻玉千斤及玉印、降魔杵等。

translations.literal: When Kuangye and the others returned, Shengtian again sent the commissioner Liu Zaisheng with a thousand jin of jade and a jade seal, demon-subduing pestle, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: After their return Shengtian sent Commissioner Liu Zaisheng with a thousand jin of jade, a jade seal, a demon-subduing pestle, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐元年，又遣使者王知鐸來。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyou of Han they again sent envoy Wang Zhiduo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyou of Later Han they sent envoy Wang Zhiduo.

sentences.zh: 高麗，本扶餘人之別種也。

translations.literal: Goryeo were originally a separate branch of the Fuyu people.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo was originally an offshoot of the Fuyu people.

sentences.zh: 其國地、君世見於唐，比他夷狄有姓氏，而其官號略可曉其義。

translations.literal: Their state's territory and rulers appear in Tang; unlike other barbarians they had surnames, and their official titles can roughly be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands and rulers appear in Tang records. Unlike other frontier peoples they used surnames, and their official titles are roughly intelligible.

sentences.zh: 當唐之末，其王姓高氏。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang their king bore the surname Gao.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Tang their royal house bore the surname Gao.

sentences.zh: 同光元年，遣使廣評侍郎韓申一、副使春部少卿樸岩來，而其國王姓名，史失不紀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang they sent envoys Broad Review Vice Minister Han Shenyi and Deputy Envoy Spring Department Junior Minister Pu Yan; the name of their king is lost from the records.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongguang they sent Broad Review Vice Minister Han Shenyi and Deputy Envoy Pu Yan of the Spring Department, but their king's name is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 至長興三年，權知國事王建遣使者來，明宗乃拜建玄菟州都督，充大義軍使，封高麗國王。

translations.literal: By the third year of Changxing Wang Jian, acting head of state affairs, sent envoys; Mingzong appointed Jian military commissioner of Xuantu Prefecture, made him commander of the Dayi Army, and enfeoffed him as king of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing acting ruler Wang Jian sent envoys. Mingzong appointed him commissioner of Xuantu, commander of the Dayi Army, and king of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 建，高麗大族也。

translations.literal: Jian was of a great Goryeo clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian came from a leading Goryeo clan.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，建卒，子武立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun Jian died and his son Wu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun Jian died and his son Wu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 乾祐四年，武卒，子昭立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianyou Wu died and his son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianyou Wu died and his son Zhao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王氏三世，終五代常來朝貢，其立也必請命中國，中國常優答之。

translations.literal: The Wang line for three generations came regularly to court with tribute throughout the Five Dynasties; on accession they always requested appointment from China, and China always responded generously.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the Wang house sent tribute throughout the Five Dynasties, always seeking Chinese confirmation on accession, which China granted generously.

sentences.zh: 其地產銅、銀，周世宗時，遣尚書水部員外郎韓彥卿以帛數千匹市銅於高麗以鑄鐵。

translations.literal: Their land produced copper and silver; in Shizong's time of Zhou they sent Ministry of Works Water Department aide Han Yanqing with several thousand bolts of silk to buy copper in Goryeo for casting iron.
translations.idiomatic: Their country produced copper and silver. Under Zhou Shizong, Han Yanqing of the Water Department was sent with thousands of bolts of silk to buy Goryeo copper for iron casting.

sentences.zh: 六年，昭遣使者貢黃銅五萬斤。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhao sent envoys with tribute of fifty thousand jin of yellow copper.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhao sent envoys with fifty thousand jin of yellow copper as tribute.

sentences.zh: 高麗俗知文字，喜讀書，昭進《別敘孝經》一卷、《越王新義》八卷、《皇靈孝經》一卷、《孝經雌圖》一卷。

translations.literal: Goryeo custom knew writing and loved books; Zhao presented one juan of Separate Narrative Classic of Filial Piety, eight juan of King Yue's New Meaning, one juan of Imperial Spirit Classic of Filial Piety, and one juan of Classic of Filial Piety Yin Chart.
translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo were literate and fond of books. Zhao presented the Separate Narrative Classic of Filial Piety, eight juan of the King of Yue's New Meaning, the Imperial Spirit Classic of Filial Piety, and the Yin Chart of the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 《別敘》，敘孔子所生及弟子事蹟；

translations.literal: The Separate Narrative recounts where Confucius was born and the deeds of his disciples;
translations.idiomatic: The Separate Narrative tells where Confucius was born and what his disciples did;

sentences.zh: 《越王新義》，以「越王」爲問目，若今「正義」；

translations.literal: the King of Yue's New Meaning takes "King of Yue" as the topic of inquiry, like today's "Correct Meaning";
translations.idiomatic: the King of Yue's New Meaning uses "King of Yue" as a framing question, like modern commentaries;

sentences.zh: 《皇靈》，述延年辟穀；

translations.literal: the Imperial Spirit describes Yan Nian's grain avoidance;
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Spirit describes Yan Nian's fasting regimen;

sentences.zh: 《雌圖》，載日食、星變。

translations.literal: the Yin Chart records solar eclipses and stellar anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: the Yin Chart records eclipses and unusual stars.

sentences.zh: 皆不經之說。

translations.literal: All are unorthodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: All were unorthodox works.

sentences.zh: 渤海，本號靺鞨，高麗之別種也。

translations.literal: Bohai were originally called Mohe, a separate branch of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai were originally known as the Mohe, an offshoot of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 唐高宗滅高麗，徙其人散處中國，置安東都護府於平壤以統治之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong of Tang destroyed Goryeo, relocated its people scattered through China, and set the Protectorate General of Andong at Pyongyang to rule them.
