translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong of Tang conquered Goryeo, resettled its people across China, and established the Andong Protectorate at Pyongyang to govern the region.

sentences.zh: 武后時，契丹攻北邊，高麗別種大乞乞仲象與靺鞨酋長乞四比羽走遼東，分王高麗故地，武后遣將擊殺乞四比羽，而乞乞仲象亦病死。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time the Khitan attacked the northern border; the Goryeo offshoot Da Qiqi Zhongxiang and the Mohe chieftain Qi Sibi Yu fled to Liaodong and divided rule of old Goryeo lands; Wu sent generals who killed Qi Sibi Yu, and Qiqi Zhongxiang also died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu the Khitan raided the north. The Goryeo chieftain Da Qiqi Zhongxiang and Mohe leader Qi Sibi Yu fled to Liaodong and divided the old Goryeo lands. Wu's generals killed Qi Sibi Yu, and Zhongxiang soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 仲象子祚榮立，因並有比羽之衆，其衆四十萬人，據挹婁，臣于唐。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang's son Zuorong succeeded, thereby absorbing Biyu's followers as well; his host numbered four hundred thousand, holding Yilou, and he submitted to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang's son Zuorong succeeded him, absorbed Biyu's people, and commanded four hundred thousand followers in Yilou, submitting to Tang.

sentences.zh: 至中宗時，置忽汗州，以祚榮爲都督，封渤海郡王，其後世遂號渤海。

translations.literal: By Zhongzong's time Hohan Prefecture was established, Zuorong made commissioner, and enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai; later generations took the name Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, Hohan Prefecture was established with Zuorong as commissioner and Prince of Bohai; his descendants took Bohai as their state name.

sentences.zh: 其貴族姓大氏，開平元年，國王大諲撰遣使者來，訖顯德常來朝貢。

translations.literal: Their nobles bore the surname Da; in the first year of Kaiping the state king Da Yinzhuan sent envoys, and down to Xiande they regularly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Their nobility bore the surname Da. In Kaiping's first year King Da Yinzhuan sent envoys, and through Xiande they regularly paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國土物產，與高麗同。

translations.literal: Their state's products were the same as Goryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: Their country's products were the same as Goryeo's.

sentences.zh: 諲撰世次、立卒，史失其紀。

translations.literal: Yinzhuan's generations, accession, and death—the records are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhuan's line, accession, and death are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨

translations.literal: Heishui Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Heishui Mohe.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨，本號勿吉。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe were originally called Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe were originally known as the Wuji.

sentences.zh: 當後魏時見中國。

translations.literal: They appear in China in the Northern Wei period.
translations.idiomatic: They appear in Chinese records during the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 其國，東至海，南界高麗，西接突厥，北鄰室韋，蓋肅慎氏之地也。

translations.literal: Their state reached the sea in the east, bordered Goryeo in the south, adjoined the Turks in the west, and neighbored the Shiwei in the north—land of the Sushen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Their country reached the sea in the east, bordered Goryeo in the south, met the Turks in the west, and neighbored the Shiwei in the north—the old land of the Sushen.

sentences.zh: 其衆分爲數十部，而黑水靺鞨最處其北，尤勁悍，無文字之記。

translations.literal: Their people were divided into several dozen tribes; the Heishui Mohe were farthest north and especially fierce, with no written records.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into dozens of tribes; the Heishui Mohe lived farthest north, were especially fierce, and kept no written records.

sentences.zh: 其兵，角弓、楛矢。

translations.literal: Their weapons were horn bows and wooden arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They fought with horn bows and wooden-shafted arrows.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，黑水兀兒遣使者來，其後常來朝貢，自登州泛海出青州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang the Heishui Wuer sent envoys; afterward they came regularly with tribute, sailing from Deng Prefecture by sea to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongguang the Heishui leader Wuer sent envoys. Thereafter they came regularly by sea from Deng Prefecture to Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，黑水胡獨鹿亦遣使來。

translations.literal: The next year the Heishui Hudulu also sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Heishui leader Hudulu also sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 兀兒、胡獨鹿若其兩部酋長，各以使來。

translations.literal: Wuer and Hudulu were probably chieftains of two tribes, each sending envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wuer and Hudulu were likely chiefs of two tribes, each sending his own mission.

sentences.zh: 而其部族、世次、立卒，史皆失其紀。

translations.literal: As for their tribes, generations, accession, and death, the records are all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribal divisions, genealogies, and successions are all lost.

sentences.zh: 至長興三年，胡獨鹿卒，子桃李花立，嘗請命中國，後遂不復見云。

translations.literal: By the third year of Changxing Hudulu died and his son Taolihua succeeded; he once requested appointment from China, but afterward was no longer seen, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing Hudulu died and his son Taolihua succeeded, once seeking Chinese confirmation, but afterward disappeared from the record.

sentences.zh: 南詔蠻

translations.literal: Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 南詔蠻，見於唐。

translations.literal: Nanzhao appears in Tang records.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao appears in Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 其國在漢故永昌郡之東、姚州之西。

translations.literal: Their state lay east of Han's old Yongchang commandery and west of Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their kingdom lay east of the old Han Yongchang commandery and west of Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 僖宗幸蜀，募能使南詔者，得宗室子李龜年及徐虎、虎侄藹，乃以龜年爲使，虎爲副，藹爲判官，使南詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu he sought men who could go to Nanzhao, found the imperial clansman Li Guinian and Xu Hu and Hu's nephew Ai, and made Guinian envoy, Hu deputy, and Ai vice commissioner to Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu he sought envoys to Nanzhao and found the imperial clansman Li Guinian, Xu Hu, and Hu's nephew Ai. Guinian was made envoy, Hu deputy, and Ai vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 南詔所居曰苴絺城，龜年等不至苴絺，至善闡，得其要約與唐爲甥舅。

translations.literal: Nanzhao's seat was called Juzhi city; Guinian and the others did not reach Juzhi but went only to Shanchan, obtaining a pact to be uncle and nephew with Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao's capital was Juzhi. Guinian's party did not reach it but stopped at Shanchan, where they secured a pact of uncle-nephew relations with Tang.

sentences.zh: 僖宗許以安化公主妻之，南詔大喜，遣人隨龜年求公主。

translations.literal: Xizong promised the Princess of Anhua in marriage; Nanzhao was greatly pleased and sent men with Guinian to request the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong promised the Princess of Anhua in marriage. Nanzhao rejoiced and sent men back with Guinian to fetch her.

sentences.zh: 已而黃巢敗，收復長安，僖宗東還，乃止。

translations.literal: Soon Huang Chao was defeated, Chang'an recovered, and Xizong returned east—the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao was defeated and Xizong returned to Chang'an, the marriage was called off.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，魏王繼岌及郭崇韜等破蜀，得王衍時所俘南詔蠻數十人，又得徐藹，自言嘗使南詔，乃矯詔還其所俘，遣藹等持金帛招撫南詔，諭以威德，南詔不納。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang Prince of Wei Jiji and Guo Chongtao and others defeated Shu, obtained several dozen Nanzhao captives from Wang Yan's time, and also Xu Ai, who said he had once been envoy to Nanzhao; they forged an edict to return the captives and sent Ai and others with gold and silk to win over Nanzhao, instructing them in power and virtue—Nanzhao did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang Prince Jiji of Wei and Guo Chongtao conquered Shu, recovered dozens of Nanzhao captives taken under Wang Yan, and found Xu Ai, who claimed prior service as envoy. They forged an edict returning the captives and sent Ai with gold and silk to win Nanzhao over—but Nanzhao refused.

sentences.zh: 至明宗時，巂州山后兩林百蠻都鬼主、右武衛大將軍李卑晚，遣大鬼主傅能何華來朝貢，明宗拜卑晚甯遠將軍，又以大渡河南山前邛州六姓都鬼主懷安郡王勿定摽莎爲定遠將軍。

translations.literal: By Mingzong's time the Xizhou mountain rear Two Forests Hundred Barbarians paramount ghost lord and Right Martial Guard senior general Li Beiwan sent the great ghost lord Fu Nenghua to pay tribute; Mingzong appointed Beiwan General Who Pacifies the Distance, and also made the Qiongzhou Six Clans paramount ghost lord south of the Dadu River, Prince of Huai'an Wuding Biaosha, General Who Fixes the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong, Li Beiwan, paramount lord of the Two Forests tribes behind Xizhou and a Right Martial Guard general, sent the great ghost lord Fu Nenghua with tribute. Mingzong made Beiwan a General Who Pacifies the Distance and appointed Wuding Biaosha of the Six Clans south of the Dadu River a General Who Fixes the Distance.

sentences.zh: 明年遣左金吾衛將軍烏昭遠爲入蠻國信使，昭遠不能達而還。

translations.literal: The next year they sent Left Golden Crow Guard general Wu Zhaoyuan as credentialed envoy into the barbarian state; Zhaoyuan could not reach it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Left Golden Crow Guard general Wu Zhaoyuan was sent as envoy to the barbarian lands but could not get through and returned.

sentences.zh: 牂牁蠻，在辰州西千五百里，以耕植爲生，而無城郭聚落，有所攻擊，則相屯聚。

translations.literal: The Zhangke barbarians were fifteen hundred li west of Chen Prefecture; they lived by farming but had no walled towns or settlements—when attacked they gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangke lived fifteen hundred li west of Chen Prefecture, farming without walled towns; when threatened they gathered for defense.

sentences.zh: 刻木爲契。

translations.literal: They carved wood for contracts.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded agreements by carving wood.

sentences.zh: 其首領姓謝氏，其名見於唐。

translations.literal: Their chieftains bore the surname Xie; their names appear in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs bore the surname Xie and appear in Tang records.

sentences.zh: 至天成二年嘗一至，其使者曰清州八郡刺史宋朝化，冠帶如中國，貢草豆蔻二萬個、硃砂五百兩、蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: By the second year of Tiancheng they came once; their envoy was called Qingzhou Eight-Districts Prefect Song Chaohua, cap and belt like China's, with tribute of twenty thousand cardamom pods, five hundred liang of cinnabar, and two hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng they came once. Their envoy, Qingzhou Eight-Districts Prefect Song Chaohua, dressed in Chinese style and brought twenty thousand cardamom pods, five hundred liang of cinnabar, and two hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 昆明，在黔州西南三千里外，地產羊馬。

translations.literal: Kunming was three thousand li southwest of Qian Prefecture; the land produced sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kunming lay three thousand li southwest of Qian Prefecture and produced sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 其人椎髻、跣足、披氈，其首領披虎皮。

translations.literal: Their people wore topknots, went barefoot, and draped felt; their chieftains wore tiger skins.
translations.idiomatic: They wore topknots, went barefoot, and wrapped themselves in felt; their chiefs wore tiger skins.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，嘗一至，其首領號昆明大鬼主，羅殿王、普露靜王九部落，各遣使者來，使者號若土，附牂牁以來。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng they came once; their chieftain was styled Great Ghost Lord of Kunming; the Luo Hall King, Pulujing King, and nine tribes each sent envoys; envoys were called Ruotu and came attached to the Zhangke mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng they came once. Their chief styled himself Great Ghost Lord of Kunming; the Luo Hall King, Pulujing King, and nine tribes each sent envoys called Ruotu, arriving with the Zhangke mission.

sentences.zh: 占城，在西南海上。

translations.literal: Champa lay on the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Champa lay on the southwestern seas.

sentences.zh: 其地方千里，東至海，西至雲南，南鄰真腦，北抵驩州。

translations.literal: Their territory was a thousand li square; east to the sea, west to Yunnan, south bordering Champa, north reaching Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm was a thousand li square, reaching the sea in the east, Yunnan in the west, Champa in the south, and Huan Prefecture in the north.

sentences.zh: 其人，俗與大食同。

translations.literal: Their people's customs were the same as the Arabs'.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs resembled those of the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 其乘，象、馬；

translations.literal: Their mounts were elephants and horses;
translations.idiomatic: They rode elephants and horses;

sentences.zh: 其食，稻米、水兕、山羊。

translations.literal: their food was rice, river rhinoceros, and mountain goats.
translations.idiomatic: their food was rice, river rhinoceros, and mountain goat.

sentences.zh: 鳥獸之奇，犀、孔雀。

translations.literal: Exotic birds and beasts included rhinoceros and peacocks.
translations.idiomatic: Among their exotic animals were rhinoceros and peacocks.

sentences.zh: 自前世未嘗通中國。

translations.literal: From former ages they had never had contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: They had had no contact with China in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 顯德五年，其國王因德漫遣使者莆訶散來，貢猛火油八十四瓶、薔薇水十五瓶，其表以貝多葉書之，以香木爲函。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiande their king Yindeman sent envoy Puhesan with tribute of eighty-four bottles of fierce fire oil and fifteen bottles of rose water; the memorial was written on pattra leaves in a casket of fragrant wood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiande King Yindeman sent envoy Puhesan with eighty-four bottles of Greek fire and fifteen of rose water. The memorial was written on palm leaves in a box of fragrant wood.

sentences.zh: 猛火油以灑物，得水則出火。

translations.literal: Fierce fire oil, when sprinkled on things, bursts into flame on contact with water.
translations.idiomatic: Greek fire, when sprinkled on objects, ignites on contact with water.

sentences.zh: 薔薇水，雲得自西域，以灑衣，雖敝而香不滅。

translations.literal: Rose water, it is said, came from the Western Regions; sprinkled on clothing, though worn out the fragrance does not fade.
translations.idiomatic: Rose water, said to come from the Western Regions, was sprinkled on clothing so that even when threadbare the scent lingered.

sentences.zh: 五代，四夷見中國者，遠不過于闐、占城。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties, of the four barbarians who appeared in China, none were farther than Khotan and Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier peoples who reached China in the Five Dynasties, none came from farther than Khotan and Champa.

sentences.zh: 史之所紀，其西北頗詳，而東南尤略，蓋其遠而罕至，且不爲中國利害云。

translations.literal: What the histories record is rather detailed for the northwest but especially sparse for the southeast—because they were far and rarely came, and were of no profit or harm to China, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Histories record the northwest in some detail but the southeast only sketchily, because those lands were distant, visitors rare, and of little consequence to China—or so it is said.
